# `path-edges`

Synthetic filesystem edge cases for traversal tests (plan Sections 15, 17/P2.1).
This directory holds the fixture *definition*; the tree itself is generated
deterministically at test time by `build_path_edges` in
`crates/ghosttrace-core/tests/capture_scope.rs`, because Git cannot track FIFOs
or sockets and generated trees keep byte-identity problems out of history.

## Generated shape

```
<root>/
├── plain.txt                  ordinary file
├── alias.txt                  hardlink of plain.txt (one identity, two paths)
├── nested/deep/deeper/
│   └── hidden.log             ordinary file below the root
├── escape -> ../outside/target.txt   symlink escaping the root
├── loop -> nested             symlink loop back into the root
├── pipe                       FIFO (never read as a file)
└── .probe.sock                Unix socket (never read as a file)
```

## Expected traversal outcome

| Path | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `plain.txt` | captured | file |
| `alias.txt` | captured (hardlink alias) | one identity, second path observation |
| `nested/deep/deeper/hidden.log` | captured | file |
| `escape` | captured, not followed | symlink target is metadata only |
| `loop` | captured, not followed | symlink loop never descended |
| `pipe`, `.probe.sock` | unsupported | special files are never read |

## Native-path edges also exercised

- invalid UTF-8 name (`rep\xff ort.txt`) — bytes preserved exactly
- Unicode-distinct names (`café.txt` vs `cafe\u{301}.txt`) — no normalization
- deep chains (24 levels) — bounded by depth cap with disclosure
- read-only subtree (mode 0700/0000 as an ordinary user) — permission gaps

The permission test skips itself under root, because privilege makes the check
vacuous; that skip is reported by the test, not hidden.
